messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test case testAddNonComparable attempts to add a plain Object instance to the Frequency instance using addValue(Object). The test expects this to fail with an IllegalArgumentException. From the source code:

- The deprecated addValue(Object v) method simply casts the input Object v to Comparable<?> and calls addValue(Comparable<?> v).
- The addValue(Comparable<?> v) method checks if the incoming Comparable is an Integer and converts it to Long, otherwise it uses it as-is.
- It then tries to get the current count from freqTable, which is a TreeMap presumably keyed by Comparable objects.
- If freqTable.get(obj) throws a ClassCastException (which can happen with TreeMap if obj is not comparable or differs in comparison logic from existing keys), the method catches this and throws an IllegalArgumentException with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

The bug report suggests that the first call to addValue(Object) with a non-comparable Object wrongly succeeded in the past and caused later failures, but looking at this code, the key point is:

- addValue(Object) does not check whether the Object is actually Comparable before casting and passing it on.
- This can cause a ClassCastException inside addValue(Comparable<?> v) when freqTable.get(obj) tries to compare a non-comparable key with existing keys in the TreeMap.

Therefore, the bug is that addValue(Object) accepts any Object, even if it is not Comparable, allowing the first add to proceed without error, but eventually causing failures on subsequent additions or operations.

The correct behavior would be that addValue(Object) should either reject non-Comparable objects immediately, throwing IllegalArgumentException without delegating to addValue(Comparable<?>), or perform a type check and handle accordingly.

Summary: The bug occurs because addValue(Object) method casts the Object to Comparable<?> without verifying the Object is indeed Comparable, leading to runtime ClassCastException caught and converted to IllegalArgumentException only when interacting with the freqTable. The initial addition of a non-Comparable Object incorrectly succeeds, violating expected API constraints, causing further failures later.

This diagnosis explains the test case failure and aligns with the bug report details.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Comparable<?>)
